name: Device Tree Explorer
blurb: a DTS with its includes merged into one tree, phandles resolved, addresses translated and conflicts found
intro: Merges a board .dts with its #include'd .dtsi files and overlays the way cpp, dtc and fdt apply do, and shows the resulting tree: every property with the file that set it and what it overrode, phandle references as links, and each reg translated through the parents' ranges to a CPU physical address. It flags overlapping regions, two devices on one I2C/SPI address, pins muxed twice, undefined labels, wrong cell counts and okay nodes under a disabled parent.

usage: Give the main .dts text (dts) and its file name (main_name), every .dtsi it includes and any overlays as files [{name, kind: include|overlay, text}], and optionally node (a label or path) to inspect. It returns counts, a Findings table (overlapping reg, duplicate I2C/SPI addresses, pins muxed by two enabled devices, undefined labels, #cells mismatches, ranges misses, okay nodes under disabled parents), the CPU physical address map, the chosen node's merged properties with which file set each one, and the whole merged tree as DTS text. Use it to review a board device tree before building, or to find which file really sets a property.
sources: Devicetree Specification v0.4 (devicetree.org): §2.3.4 status, §2.3.5 #address-cells/#size-cells defaults, §2.3.6 reg, §2.3.8 ranges, §2.4 interrupts
